title: Dynamic Reservoir Calibrator for Request Surge Mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS with heterogeneous request sizes we observe repeated tail-latency spikes and KV cache churn leading to GPU OOMs on a subset of nodes. Current static micro-batch thresholds and single-signal backpressure do not adapt quickly enough to workload shifts (burstiness, long-context requests), causing either under-utilized GPUs or unsafe memory pressure that forces evictions and degrades quality.

Goal: Implement a Dynamic Reservoir Calibrator (DRC) that continuously estimates available GPU headroom and KV cache pressure at per-shard granularity and adjusts micro-batching admission thresholds + progressive backpressure signals in real-time. The DRC should: (1) reduce tail latency and OOM frequency during spikes, (2) increase throughput when safe, (3) integrate with existing KV eviction policies, and (4) expose metrics and knobs in Console for canary rollouts.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- 95th token latency reduced by >=15% in synthetic 4x burst test compared to mainline (baseline: 95th=230ms).
- GPU OOM events reduced by >=90% during 2x QPS sustained test with mixed long/short sequences.
- End-to-end request success rate for P1 customers remains >=99.95% during 99th percentile QPS.
- System exposes per-shard headroom_score, kv_hotness_index, and admission_threshold in telemetry and has dashboard + alerting configured.

Scope: DRC includes: (A) lightweight online estimator that fuses GPU free pages, slab fragmentation, KV cache hit rates, and recent micro-batch occupancy to a single headroom_score; (B) sigmoid-based scaling policy that maps headroom_score to microbatch_size cap and admission timeout; (C) staged backpressure signals (soft deny, delay, hard deny) broadcast via existing admission-controller bus; (D) integration tests, perf benchmarks, and Console controls for rollout and canary.

Out of scope: kernel-level allocator changes, quantization pipeline optimizations, and long-term auto-tuning model training (this ticket focuses on an online heuristic engine + telemetry).
notes: Design doc: iterative estimator combining EWMA of free_gpu_pages, fragmentation_ratio and kv_eviction_rate; use 30s and 300s windows for short/long trends.
Prior work: leverages admission-controller and token-slot leasing code from ENG-88021 and headroom predictor from ENG-100823.
Controller policy: use smooth scaling (sigmoid) to avoid oscillation. Parameters exposed: slope(β), mid-point(μ), min_threshold, max_threshold, emergency_hard_limit.
KV integration: when headroom_score < 0.25, increase kv_eviction_aggressiveness for low-priority keys and mark large-context KV entries for prefetch-eviction.
Telemetry: add headroom_score, kv_hotness_index, eviction_rate_1m, microbatch_fill_percentile per shard. Tie alerts to headroom_score < 0.15 for > 60s.
Risk: aggressive eviction can cause model quality regression. Mitigation: progressive policy, canary on non-production traffic with quality eval promptset.
Fallback: if DRC misbehaves, route node to maintenance and revert admission_policy to static defaults; add automatic circuit-breaker if OOMs spike after rollout.
